subject.title: Add a retraction window for forwarded exec approvals (agent-cancellable hold before prompt delivery)

question: Should OpenClaw add an opt-in exec approval hold/retract contract, and where should that contract live across Gateway, native channel runtimes, and Codex integration?
rationale: The request changes approval timing, execution-denial semantics, public config, Gateway RPC/API shape, and dependency-facing Codex/native behavior, so automation should not choose the product boundary alone.

options.title: Design Gateway-owned hold/retract
options.body: Add `approvals.exec.holdMs`, a reviewed `exec.approval.retract` contract, fail-open delivery, fail-closed execution, audit logs, docs, and coverage across forwarded/native approval paths.

options.title: Reject hold/retract for now
options.body: Keep instant forwarding as the approval safety model and address noise through allowlists, target routing, or agent command-generation improvements instead.

options.title: Narrow to harness-side suppression
options.body: Explore whether Codex/native harnesses can avoid creating abandoned approval requests before Gateway delivery rather than adding a new Gateway retraction API.

recommendation.title: Design Gateway-owned hold/retract
recommendation.body: Add `approvals.exec.holdMs`, a reviewed `exec.approval.retract` contract, fail-open delivery, fail-closed execution, audit logs, docs, and coverage across forwarded/native approval paths.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter Steinberger has the strongest history across approval forwarding, Gateway approval safety, and routing refactors that this decision would affect.
